wire.settings.asks.description.note: Says the setting applies immediately everywhere (terminal UI, desktop app, phone). Do not imply a restart.

wire.settings.asks.title.note: Section heading for the queued-question settings. 'Ask' is the product noun for a question an agent queues for the user; keep it short and consistent with the ask bar/list vocabulary.

wire.settings.asks_lapsed_visible_for.ch.note: Measured from the ask's deadline, not from when it was asked.
A duration; use the locale's natural form for one hour.
A duration of 24 hours (not 'one day'): the four choices read as a ladder.
Measured from the ask's deadline; '(default)' marks the shipped value, keep it.
The ask disappears the moment its deadline passes.

wire.settings.asks_lapsed_visible_for.he.note: Shown as '<help> · default: 7d' on the settings page's 74-cell detail line at 80 columns; keep the help within 58 cells so the default clause fits. Display only: hiding never answers or deletes the ask.

wire.settings.asks_lapsed_visible_for.la.note: Row label; 29 cells is the settings page's label budget (_LABEL_BUDGET). 'Timed-out' = the ask's deadline passed with no answer. The row only changes how long such an ask stays SHOWN; it does not change whether the agent hears a late answer.

wire.settings.session_scratchpad.title.note: Section heading for the scratchpad size cap. 'Scratchpad' is the product noun for a session's own scratch area (scratchpad://); keep it one word.

wire.settings.session_scratchpad.descrip.note: Says the cap applies to each session's own scratch area and is checked per write, not at launch. Do not imply a restart.

wire.settings.session_scratchpad_max_byt.note: Row label; 29 cells is the settings page's label budget. It names the MAXIMUM bytes one session's scratchpad may hold (not the current size) and carries the unit because the desktop collapses help behind a disclosure (design D1). Every locale must fit the same 29-cell budget.
Carries both bounds and the default because the page paints help but not min/max. Units are bytes; use the binary prefixes MiB/GiB, not MB/GB.

wire.settings.remote_compute.title.note: Section heading for the remote-compute preview. 'Compute' is the product noun for where a run executes; keep it short enough for the settings header's 34-cell value column.

wire.settings.remote_compute.description.note: Desktop-only section header sentence. Must say the feature is a PREVIEW and that work runs on Radient-hosted compute. 'Mesh network' is the product term for the user's device network; do not translate it as a social network or a Wi-Fi network.

wire.settings.remote_compute_enabled.lab.note: Boolean row label under the Remote compute section. Keep under 29 cells.

wire.settings.remote_compute_enabled.hel.note: Must state this is a preview, that it sends the user's work to Radient-hosted compute, and that the run is bound to ONE of the user's mesh networks — the tenant claim. The old wording said 'in your mesh network', which read as containment and is not what the slice enforces. 'Radient' is a product name: keep it unchanged. Keep near 67 cells (en is 66; the 80x24 detail line sheds longer copy, so stay within 74).

wire.settings.remote_compute_enabled.cho.note: What ON means: remote runs are allowed. Lowercase, about 20 cells.
What OFF means: work stays on this machine. Lowercase, about 10 cells.
